title: Editorial Spreads
summary: A black-and-white editorial interpretation of “Alien Invasion or Sleep Paralysis?” exploring the uneasy overlap between waking life, dreams, and perceived encounters.

hero.alt: Looping preview of the editorial spread.

overview.challenge: How can a magazine spread make the uncertain state between waking and dreaming feel tangible? The article ‘Alien Invasion or Sleep Paralysis?’ offered a way to explore the unsettling overlap between sleep paralysis and stories of alien abduction.
overview.solution: I used stark black-and-white contrast, distorted display type, and tightly controlled body copy to balance hallucination-like disruption with editorial clarity.
overview.outcome: The finished spreads keep the imagined presence partly obscured, using scale, alignment, and negative space to sustain tension while keeping the article readable.
overview._notes: Copy refined to reflect the documented project concept.

blocks.label: 01 — Research
blocks.body: I chose "Alien Invasion or Sleep Paralysis?" because the topic fascinated me and offered a chance to explore the visual confusion between two surreal experiences.
blocks.alt: Research references for the editorial spread.
blocks.heading: Between waking and dreaming

blocks.label: 02 — Sketches
blocks.alt: Sketches and early layout studies for the editorial spread.
blocks.heading: Testing tension and hierarchy
blocks.body: Early layout studies tested the balance between disrupted typography and a stable reading path. I explored scale, cropping, and the placement of shadowy imagery, refining the composition so the spread feels psychologically unstable without becoming difficult to follow.

blocks.label: 03 — Concept development
blocks.alt: Concept development for the editorial spread.
blocks.heading: Keeping the threat unresolved
blocks.body: The concept developed through contrast: chaotic, distorted display type evokes the half-conscious experience, while the body text remains structured. The alien form and shadow are never fully revealed, allowing the reader to feel uncertainty rather than receive a literal explanation.

blocks.label: 04 — Final
blocks.caption: Final editorial spread: distortion and structure share the page.
